summary: The Win64 C ABI and typed confined faults, host-arch native targeting (linux-arm64), builtin-shadow and fn-value fixes, the CLI duplicate-flag recovery, the same-call borrow diagnostic fix, and truly cold benchmark lanes -- on the stdlib-v0.64.7 pin.

highlights.title: Win64 C ABI aggregates + typed confined faults
highlights.text: Externs now lower by-value aggregates and returns with the MSVC C convention on x86_64-pc-windows-msvc (a 16B by-value aggregate passes as a pointer operand, a 16B return uses sret), and raw `Int as fn(..)` casts use the same C-lowered fn-pointer type. SysV/AArch64 keep the internal convention until each is validated. Confined faults are no longer silent: the runtime records the permanent fault, prints an always-on typed diagnostic, and exits 70 unless the program acknowledges via `xiom.error.take_fault()`; retries are restricted to the guard-page transient class, so side effects run once.

highlights.title: Host-arch native targeting (linux-arm64 enabler)
highlights.text: `Target::Native` now follows the host architecture instead of assuming x86_64-linux, and the toolchain resolver carries the linux-arm64 asset names/sums. The arm64 release leg and the packages edge lane can target the host directly.

highlights.title: Builtins stop shadowing declarations
highlights.text: Scalar `.hash()` and the Mutex barrier no longer shadow user/stdlib declarations: `Int.hash`/`Bool.hash` and `xiom.sync.Mutex[T]` resolve to the declaration in runtime, static, and IR paths.

highlights.title: fn-value trio on the hook seam
highlights.text: Module-global fn-typed vars get their thunk emitted at definition, fn-typed struct fields keep the uniform ENV representation (adjacent fn fields no longer overwrite each other), and fn-typed aliases used as callable parameters dispatch through the resolved signature instead of access-violating.

highlights.title: CLI duplicate value flags recover cleanly
highlights.text: A duplicated value flag after the positional (`xiom file.xi --timeout 900 --timeout 900`) now exits 2 with a clean diagnostic instead of a clap panic; default-less flag reads never touch the fallback matches.

highlights.title: Borrow diagnostics: one borrow site, one warning
highlights.text: E001 no longer reports a false move when a by-value argument is followed by a borrow of the same local in a later argument of the same call. Genuine cross-statement reuse still warns. The `--check` borrow-pass parity gap is recorded as a residual.

highlights.title: Benchmark cold lanes stay cold
highlights.text: `--no-cache` now disables the persistent catalog index and catalog-body check caches (read and write) in the compile, AOT-run, and in-process JIT paths. A lock proves the control run writes `checkbodies.txt` while cold runs write neither `checkbodies.txt` nor `catidx.txt`.

known_issues: Int128 division/modulo in a Vec loop can access-violate (m360, in flight).
A capture-frames probe can hang on the run leg (m366, minimized snippet requested).
Send/Sync markers are declared and auto-derived but not yet enforced on spawn captures (m363, queued).
Deep container equality remains pointer identity (carried from v0.64.6).
The dependency-object cache key is consumer-specific, and a HIT does not verify object existence under concurrent builds (m365, queued).
